start_here: Say to your AI: "Switch on workflow:keep-the-use-case-catalog-current with runs_connection <the vault name of the database that holds your workflow rows>, catalog_connection <the vault name of the database that holds your use-case rows>, catalog_table <your use-case table> links_table <your link table> and id_prefix <the id prefix your catalog rows use for new rows>." It then links every use-case row to the workflow that serves it each day and each time a workflow row changes.
no_lists_because: The sweep reads the workflow rows and writes the use-case table and its link table, all in the databases the person already keeps. No list of the person's is read or written.
instructions: 1. Name the vault connection of the workflow-rows database (runs_connection), the vault connection of the use-case database (catalog_connection), the two table names (catalog_table, links_table) and the id prefix for new rows (id_prefix).
2. Install the catalog function once in the use-case database from use-case-catalog/apply-delta.sql in the workflows folder (it is a function, not a list, and needs no rows).

3. Create the sweep mark once in the workflows database: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS use_case_sweep_marks (name text PRIMARY KEY, swept_through timestamptz NOT NULL); then INSERT INTO use_case_sweep_marks (name, swept_through) VALUES ('use-case-catalog', now()) ON CONFLICT (name) DO NOTHING.
4. Switch the daily wake and the row-change trigger on for workflow:keep-the-use-case-catalog-current with those names as its input.
5. Read the counts the sweep answers (linked_touched, new_rows, internal, gaps_added) and the use-case rows it wrote.
